Section 1311 of the FY1987 defense authorization. It created U.S. Special Operations Command as a unified combatant command with its own budget line and a civilian assistant secretary to oversee it.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: 100 Stat. 3816](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/100/3816){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 10 U.S.C. 167](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/10/167?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Established U.S. Special Operations Command under a four-star commander.
- Gave the command service-like authority to train, equip, and budget for special operations forces.
- Created the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Special Operations and Low-Intensity Conflict.
- Listed special operations activities, including civil affairs and psychological operations.

## Why it matters

Congress imposed it over Pentagon resistance to protect special operations from neglect by the services. It completes the reforms of the [Goldwater-Nichols Act](goldwater-nichols-1986.qmd) and is an early case of [the annual NDAA](ndaa-annual.qmd) being used for structural change.

## Current status

In force as amended.
